# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-04__20-11-34`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to
> three healthy members with the existing keys intact.

## Environment

- Systems: **3 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **provider default**
- Control node: **node1**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-rhel7__o9MmSco`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster on node1/node2/node3, wrote application keys, directly demonstrated the required healthy-baseline -> node3-loss-with-quorum-preserved -> replacement-member-restored-healthy transition with matching raft indices and intact keys, and additionally completed the mandatory per-node restart protocol with clear boot-identity changes and full post-reboot recovery on all three nodes. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The only hygiene concern is unremoved etcd installation artifacts left in /tmp on all three nodes, a minor, low-risk residue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.900 | 56/10 (+3 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Establish a three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** etcd 3.5.17 was installed fresh on all three nodes (none had it), a systemd unit and config were created, firewall ports 2379/2380 opened, and the cluster was bootstrapped. Member list shows all three members 'started' and healthy (cmd-e5431965b0504d8c). Four application keys were written from node1 and confirmed readable from node3's own endpoint (cmd-07a8ebc2703749e1, cmd-e01fae350f51481e), directly showing the healthy 3-member baseline with data present on all members.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ab9908a15c92499d`, `cmd-e5431965b0504d8c`, `cmd-07a8ebc2703749e1`, `cmd-e01fae350f51481e`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Handle permanent loss of the node3 member (data unrecoverable) while preserving cluster quorum/availability
  - **Why:** node3's etcd was stopped/disabled and /var/lib/etcd deleted, simulating unrecoverable data loss (cmd-79c2521caeda443a). The dead member was then removed from the cluster via etcdctl issued from node1, and the remaining node1+node2 pair was directly confirmed healthy afterward, showing quorum was preserved during the disruption (cmd-2e2579a2f2394dff). This demonstrates the required healthy-baseline -> disruption -> still-available transition for the surviving members.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-79c2521caeda443a`, `cmd-2e2579a2f2394dff`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 host, returning the cluster to 3 healthy members with existing keys intact
  - **Why:** A new member was registered via `member add` and node3 was reconfigured with `initial-cluster-state: existing` and restarted (cmd-f339cac8d7a04364, cmd-529c7418b6204595). Post-replacement, the member list shows 3 'started' members with matching raft term/applied index across all endpoints (cmd-1ee77dc7820843f2), and all four original application keys were confirmed intact via node3's own client endpoint (cmd-1a826e09bb024143), directly showing full restoration to a healthy 3-member cluster with the same data.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f339cac8d7a04364`, `cmd-529c7418b6204595`, `cmd-33394b780ec94ccc`, `cmd-1ee77dc7820843f2`, `cmd-1a826e09bb024143`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence on every managed node
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, node3, a pre-restart boot_id/healthy-cluster/keys baseline was captured, `systemctl reboot` was acknowledged (connection closed), SSH was unreachable during the transition, a new distinct boot_id was observed post-restart, and etcd active state, 3-member membership, and application keys were reconfirmed after each reboot before moving to the next node. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (boot_id changed for all three nodes between snapshots).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fae327f907734989`, `cmd-d2c033c7e8f54a08`, `cmd-b80e95ffeeeb4ce9`, `cmd-aa49d60eec064c31`, `cmd-174650c3ddf842d1`, `cmd-6b3c921334ac48c1`, `cmd-788f87d9b9a44021`, `cmd-be81e8a6c326407f`, `cmd-6d61a3fd8c584ef8`, `cmd-0114d86f66b8418d`, `cmd-9c6cad4de70b4dbf`, `cmd-fd831bb387624c12`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Executor-caused mutations were reviewed chronologically. Package/service installation (binary copy, mkdir/chown, systemd unit, etcd.conf.yml) on all three nodes were necessary prerequisites. The first `systemctl enable --now etcd` attempt (cmd-40959533baea4ebd) timed out because firewall ports were not yet open; the subsequent firewall-cmd port-opening (cmd-dd36d0c5d1064b80 et al.) and the `stop etcd; rm -rf /var/lib/etcd/*; start etcd` retry (cmd-7a01701d2c3641ce et al.) on all three nodes were corrective actions needed to recover from that failed first bootstrap attempt, not gratuitous experiments — reasonable and bounded. Read-only diagnostics (nc missing, /dev/tcp probes, ping, iptables -L) caused no state change. The main unaddressed hygiene issue is leftover installation residue: the downloaded etcd.tar.gz and extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory remain in /tmp on all three nodes after task completion (visible in after_executor temporary-files diffs), which was never cleaned up. This is a low-risk, bounded residue (disk space only, no security exposure) but was retained rather than reverted. No failed services, damaged package state, or unsafe exposure were observed in the final snapshots.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-40959533baea4ebd`, `cmd-dd36d0c5d1064b80`, `cmd-7a01701d2c3641ce`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) at all lifecycle phases on all nodes, so package database integrity cannot be independently verified from this evidence.
- The node3 'permanent loss' scenario was executor-simulated (manual stop/wipe) rather than an externally injected failure, which is consistent with the task's premise but means the disruption timing and mechanism were fully executor-controlled.
- Leftover /tmp installation artifacts (etcd.tar.gz, extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64) were not cleaned up on any of the three nodes after task completion.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
